extracted.intended_audience: students, journalists, editors, and scholars of public opinion and mass media
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for creating persuasive, widely appealing political or news imagery and narratives — how to enlist interest, secure identification, and balance realism, suspense, and stereotypes for mass audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual/Tactile Lucidity
rubrics_metrics.description: No idea is lucid for practical decision until it has visual or tactile value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate abstractions into pictures or tactile terms so that an idea can function for collective decision-making; abstract reasoning alone is insufficient for enlisting practical support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Skilled Visualizers
rubrics_metrics.description: Find gifted men who can visualize for us, since people are not all endowed with the faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible employ or craft images via people who can concretely visualize complex or private perceptions; visualizers make abstract ideas communicable to a public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform Private Intuition into Communicable Images
rubrics_metrics.description: Intuitions are often private and incommunicable; social intercourse depends on communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that intuitional insight must be made pictorial or tactile to be shared; otherwise it 'sounds like a sheaf of mist' and fails to mobilize collective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification (Empathy) with the Picture
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea conveyed is not fully our own until we have identified ourselves with some aspect of the picture; identification (empathy) is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design images and narratives that allow audiences to identify with a role or aspect of the scene — identification can be subtle or overt, but it must permit the audience to 'become a character' mentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marked Handles for Popular Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: In popular representation the handles for identification are almost always marked; you know who the hero is at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mass appeal make protagonists/antagonists and moral bearings clearly recognizable; indistinct marking reduces popular uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Must Be Actively Exercised
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience must have something to do; contemplation alone is not enough — the audience must be allowed to exercise the love of struggle, suspense, and victory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct images and stories that invite active mental participation (taking sides, rooting, suspense) rather than passive appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit Universal Arousal Themes — Sex and Fighting
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two forms of exercise which far transcend all others as to ease and eagerness: sexual passion and fighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To arouse broad, cross-cultural interest use motifs related to sexual passion or conflict/struggle; these themes blend and command wide attention across social boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and Maintain Suspense
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspense constitutes the difference between masterpieces in the museum and the popular stage and screen; unfolding events that promise outcomes hold attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To increase popular appeal, depict unfolding events with stakes and uncertainty so audiences wait breathlessly for outcomes; include clear antagonism and obstacles to generate suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Recipe for Adding Suspense (Miss Patterson)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the plot lacks suspense: 1. Add an antagonist, 2. Add an obstacle, 3. Add a problem, 4. Emphasize one of the questions in the minds of the spectator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these concrete dramaturgical devices to convert inert depiction into an engaging narrative; they help translate distant or abstract issues into gripping scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance Realism and Romanticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The popular taste is to have the drama originate in a setting realistic enough to make identification plausible and to have it terminate in a setting romantic enough to be desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with familiar footholds so audiences recognize and enter the story; conclude with desirable, uplifting resolutions (true beginning / happy ending) to satisfy mass expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to or Respect Existing Stereotypes for Popular Success
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who make moving pictures ... must adhere to the stereotypes that they find, or pay the price of frustrating expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given commercial constraints and the lag time before new images can be absorbed, using established stereotypes increases odds of broad acceptance; altering stereotypes is possible but risky and slow to yield mass success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pioneers vs Managers Trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Pioneering artists who alter stereotypes are naturally depressed and angered at managers who protect investments; pioneers measure success by standards older artists never invoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize institutional pressures: innovators may sacrifice immediate mass appeal for longer-term artistic or cultural gains; producers/editors prioritize predictable audience reception and circulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propaganda Narrative Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The skilful propagandist knows that while you must start with a plausible analysis, you must not keep on analyzing — he exhausts interest in reality by a tolerably plausible beginning, and then stokes up energy for a long voyage by brandishing a passport to heaven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For persuasive mass messaging, begin with a credible situation but shift to future promises or grand outcomes to sustain enthusiasm and avoid tedium of technical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect Story Variation with Audience Composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The original story does not keep its shape and proportions. It is edited and revised by all who played with it as they heard it; consequently the more mixed the audience, the greater will be the variation in the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate that messages will be reinterpreted differently across heterogeneous audiences; larger, more diverse publics produce more abstracted and variable receptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which 'Self' Is Addressed Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: It is of great importance in the formation of any public opinion, what self is engaged — 'self-interest' determines opinion only when we know which self out of many selects and directs the interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design messages to target the particular identity/role (e.g., homeowner, patriot, family head) you intend to mobilize; the same facts framed for different selves produce different responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing Alters Emotional Intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: If two nations are disputing a piece of territory, it matters greatly whether the people regard the negotiations as a real estate deal, an attempt to humiliate them, or as a rape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame issues in terms that evoke the intended emotional registers; shifting the frame (practical property vs moral outrage) changes whether responses are tepid or 'red hot.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't Reduce Explanation to Single Economic Determinant
rubrics_metrics.description: A man's various economic contacts limit or enlarge the range of his opinions, but which of the contacts... the materialistic conception of politics cannot predict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid simplistic economic determinism when analyzing or crafting political messaging; empirical inquiry is required to discover which of a person's social/economic relations shape a particular opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Messages Must Resonate with an Audience's Stock of Stereotypes and Personal Investment
rubrics_metrics.description: No visual idea is significant to us until it has enveloped some stress of our own personality; until it releases or resists, depresses or enhances some craving of ours it remains one of the objects which do not matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that images/narratives connect to audience's preexisting concerns, cravings, or fears so the depiction feels personally consequential rather than abstract.
